title: Evaluate external test datasets vs. synthetic generator
description:
Decide which public image test datasets to wire into the test suite alongside the synthetic library generator, based on the survey in docs/research/test-image-datasets.md.

Agreed short-list test stack (2026-06-16):
- Correctness baseline: IPTC Photo Metadata Reference Images (every field self-describing).
- Edge cases / fuzzing: ianare/exif-samples (-> exif-py) + drewnoakes/metadata-extractor corpus, with Exiv2 as the read/write diff oracle.
- Volume & realism: a slice of Unsplash Lite or the YFCC100M metadata archive.
- Library structure, albums, sidecars, privacy: our synthetic generator -- nothing off-the-shelf models a personal library (folders + albums + ratings + captions + face regions + .picasa.ini/.pal/contacts.xml + mixed RAW/JPEG/HEIC/video + skewed timestamps).

Interoperability check ('how do we compare to other programs'): IPTC interoperability tests + getpmd tool, with Exiv2/metadata-extractor as reference implementations.

Out of scope / deferred: face-recognition datasets (LFW, WIDER FACE) are deferred until face-matching algorithm(s) are selected -- not part of this evaluation.

Privacy: real-photo datasets (Unsplash/YFCC/Flickr) and real Picasa libraries are local-benchmark-only; never commit their images. Committed fixtures stay fully synthetic. Any fetch helpers follow the uv/PEP-723 script convention.

Done = decision on which external sets to adopt (read-only, local-fetch) and how each complements the synthetic generator; fetch helper(s) added if adopted.
